findings.description: The implementation consumes the iterator twice – once in the sum() call and again in the dict comprehension – which results in an empty dictionary when records is a single-pass iterator such as a generator.
findings.evidence:
>>> def gen():
...     yield ('a', 1)
...     yield ('b', 3)
...
>>> candidate.allocate(gen(), 100)
{}  # Correct output should be {'a': 25, 'b': 75}

review.summary: Candidate fails to handle single-pass iterators: it consumes the input iterator twice, leaving it exhausted for the dictionary comprehension and producing an empty mapping instead of the correct allocation.
